title: Hamlet, Shakespeare
subtitle: around 1601
subject: litterature
description: Around 1601, Shakespeare wrote Hamlet, a prince hesitant about the murder of his father. Between revenge, simulated madness and “To be or not to be”, the modern hero of conscience is born.

hero.hook: A ghost, a hesitant prince, and the most famous existential question in theater.

blocks.text: To **1601**, **William Shakespeare** writes **[[Hamlet, Prince of Denmark]]**. It is not just a revenge tragedy: it is the portrait of a modern conscience, divided between action and doubt. The monologue “**To be or not to be**” has become the quintessential existential question of Western theater.

Ghosts, simulated madness, final duel: the play mixes the supernatural and psychology before its time. Hamlet is not like the classic impulsive heroes who immediately take action. He thinks too much to act quickly, and that is precisely what makes him immortal. Shakespeare here invents a character who doubts everything, including himself.

sections.title: The Elizabethan context: a theater of the world

blocks.text: Shakespeare wrote at the height of English theater, under **Elizabeth I**. The plays are performed at the **Globe Theater**, a circular wooden theater open to the sky, where rich and poor rub shoulders, standing or sitting according to their budget. The actors are all men: the female roles are played by adolescents, in accordance with the laws of the time.

blocks.caption: William Shakespeare, author of the most talked about tragedy in the world.

blocks.text: The role of Ophélie was created by a teenager whose voice had not yet changed, in accordance with the customs of the time.

blocks.caption: The Globe Theatre: Elizabethan theater stage where Hamlet won over the audience.

blocks.text: Shakespeare seeks the truth of the heart more than flat realism. Hamlet returns from studies in **[[Wittenberg]]**, the German university town cradle of the **Protestant Reformation**. In the play, Shakespeare stages a play within a play, the "Mousetrap", to trap **Claudius** and verify the king's guilt. Theater becomes a mirror of the world and an instrument of truth.

sections.title: The spiral of revenge and the weight of hesitation

blocks.text: The King of Denmark is assassinated by his brother **Claudius**, who marries Queen **Gertrude** and takes the throne. The ghost of the deceased king reveals the crime to **Hamlet**. The duty seems clear: avenge the father. But Hamlet doubts: is this specter really his father or a deceptive demon? Is revenge just in the eyes of Christian morality?

Torn between the **[[Law of retaliation]]** and the Christian conscience which condemns the murder, he feigns madness to investigate without arousing suspicion. This strategy fails: he breaks the heart of **Ophelia**, daughter of the advisor **Polonius**, and by mistake kills Polonius himself, hiding behind a carpet. The spiral leads to the final massacre at the Danish court, where almost all the main characters perish.

sections.title: The melancholy and corruption of Denmark

blocks.text: “There is something rotten in the Kingdom of Denmark. » The play breathes moral decomposition. Hamlet's language is saturated with images of disease, decay, and corpses. His **[[Melancholy in the 16th century]]** makes him brilliant but paralyzed: in Shakespeare's time, it was considered a medical mood, linked to creativity but also to inaction.

blocks.caption: Hamlet and Yorick's skull: death reminds us of the vanity of all ambition.

blocks.text: To be or not to be, that is the question.
blocks.attribution: William Shakespeare, Hamlet, act III, scene 1

blocks.text: This famous monologue questions existence itself: is it better to endure the sufferings of life or to die to escape them? To act is to get dirty in a corrupt world; not to act is to let evil triumph. Hamlet becomes the first modern hero, incapable of reconciling thought and action. The **[[Revenge and Elizabethan honor]]** partly explains its blockage: a man of honor had to avenge the offense done to his family, but this duty came into tension with the law and morality.

sections.title: Heritage and posterity of a universal myth

blocks.text: For four centuries, Hamlet has been endlessly reinterpreted. The **Romantics** of the 19th century saw the tormented artist there; **Freud** read the **[[Oedipus complex]]** there. The play talks about the loss of a parent, the darkness of the world and the painful transition to adulthood.

Its influence goes beyond the theater: cinema, opera, comics, popular psychology. Shakespeare transforms a medieval ghost story into a metaphysical investigation into human consciousness. Hamlet remains the tragedy of indecision, where thinking already becomes a form of suffering.
**Hamlet** shows that a hero can be immortal not because he acts quickly, but because he doubts deeply. Here Shakespeare invents the modernity of theater: to think is already to suffer.
